title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
abstract: arXiv:2610.30128v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Existing sequential recommenders usually allocate a fixed computational budget to every item in a user's interaction history, regardless of the item's contribution to the final prediction. We challenge this de facto design with two diagnostic findings. (1) Non-uniform computational need: items within the same sequence vary drastically in how much computation they require. Most converge after shallow processing while a critical minority only stabilizes at full depth. (2) Suboptimality of fixed allocation: given oracle access to the target item, a non-uniform depth assignment consistently outranks the fixed one, indicating that existing uniform computation both wastes capacity on already-converged items and sacrifices overall recommendation quality. translated_title: 在关键之处深入思考：面向序列推荐的物品级自适应递归
translated_abstract: 现有的序列推荐模型通常为用户交互历史中的每个物品分配固定的计算预算，而不考虑该物品对最终预测的贡献。我们通过两项诊断性发现对这一事实上的设计提出挑战。（1）计算需求的不均匀性：同一序列中不同物品所需的计算量差异极大，大多数物品经过浅层处理即可收敛，而少数关键物品只有在完整深度下才能稳定。（2）固定分配的次优性：即使能够理想地获取目标物品信息，非均匀的深度分配也始终优于固定分配，这表明现有的均匀计算既在已收敛的物品上浪费了计算能力，又牺牲了整体推荐质量。这些观察促使计算方式从固定深度转向物品级自适应推理。为此，我们提出了LoopRec。LoopRec递归地应用一个权重共享的单一模块……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 提出LoopRec，一种针对序列推荐的物品级自适应递归方法，根据每个物品的实际计算需求动态分配递归深度，取代固定计算预算，从而既节省计算资源又提升整体推荐质量。
en_tdlr: LoopRec proposes item-level adaptive recursion for sequential recommendation, dynamically allocating computational depth to each item based on its actual needs instead of a fixed budget, thereby saving computation while improving overall recommendation quality.
